method: Every page carrying an in-scope string was rendered whole at 110 dpi with music_pages.py render and read; every in-scope line was then re-read in a PyMuPDF clip at 300-400 dpi, and characters in doubt at 500-900 dpi: apostrophes (all curly ’), the dashes in 'bars 1–8', 'bars 1–4' and '16–bar' (HL Q1, en dash) against '16-bar' (HL Q3, hyphen), 'God-awful', 'Fair-Haired' and 'eight-bar' (hyphens), the cadence dashes in OL Q4 (measured at 900 dpi: a 114 px bar, about 0.85 em, an em dash), the superscripts in AA¹BB¹, the flat in 'B♭ major', and full stops after 'Excerpt N'. The booklets' text layers are glyph-shifted and were not used as a source (one plain line of the OL listening layer, 'Excerpt 1' on page 8, was looked at afterwards only to confirm the missing full stop). I typed my own transcription of every in-scope string from the renders without copying the reading file, then diffed it against the file by machine. Conventions applied: a printed bullet in a context string is '\n• '; composing bullet lines are joined by ' • '; a heading or line printed without a bullet is joined by a space; a tick box is '□ '. Q5 B(i)-(iv) (HL) carry no questionContext or excerptLine (null); their printed lead-in is checked as grid.stem. Where excerptLine is null (Q2 and Q3 in both files) the page prints no excerpt heading, so the null was checked and matches. The elective booklet (2019-hl-007) is out of scope and was not read. Every verdict is against the reading file as it stood when this record was written (2019-hl.json modified 20:43:17, 2019-ol.json modified 20:53:42 on 19 Nov 2026); 2019-ol.json changed while the sweep was running (Q2(a) and Q4 bullets removed), and those two entries were re-checked against the new strings.
